chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Yazeed al-Kunasi, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who married during her waiting period. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she married during the waiting period of a divorce where the husband has the right of return, then upon her is stoning; and if she married during a waiting period where the husband does not have the right of return, then upon her is the penalty (hadd) of the unmarried adulterer; and if she married during the waiting period after the death of her husband, before the expiry of four months and ten days, then there is no stoning upon her, and upon her is one hundred lashes.'

I said, 'What is your view if that was from her due to ignorance?' He said, 'There is no woman today from the Muslim women except that she knows that upon her is a waiting period in divorce or death, and indeed the women of the pre-Islamic period used to know that.' I said, 'So if she knew that upon her is a waiting period, and she did not know how much it is?' He said, 'When she knew that upon her is the waiting period, the proof was necessitated upon her, so she should ask until she knows.'
ai.seo_question: What are the different penalties for a woman who marries during her waiting period (Iddah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) delineates the specific hadd penalties for a woman contracting a new marriage during her iddah, distinguishing between the severity of stoning (rajm) for divorce with right of return and flogging for other cases. The Imam emphasizes that general knowledge of the obligation to observe iddah suffices to establish liability, rendering ignorance of the precise duration insufficient for exemption. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that 'ignorance of the law' is not a valid defense when the core duty is known, reflecting the transition from pre-Islamic customs to structured Islamic legal accountability.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Yazeed Al Kunasy who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about a woman who married whilst being in her waiting period. Heasws said: ‘If she has married during a waiting period of a divorce, and for her husband is the (right of) return, so upon her would be the stoning; and if she has married during a waiting period, there not being the (right of) return for husband, so upon her would be the Penalty (Hadd) of the unmarried adulterer; and if she has married during her waiting period from after the death of her husband, before the expiry of four months and ten days, so there would not be stoning upon her, and upon her would be one hundred lashes’.

I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view, if that was from her due to ignorance’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is none from a woman today, from the Muslim women, except that she knows that upon her is a waiting period regarding a divorce, or death (of her husband), and the women during the pre-Islamic period used to know that’. I said, ‘So if she knew that upon her is a waiting period, and she did not know how much it was?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When she knew that upon her is the waiting period, the proof was necessitated upon her, so she should have asked until she had known’.
